items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001

ctx.x: Roy had quite a competitive spirit, didn’t he?

I’ve never played with anyone that loved to play as much as him. Never. And my greatest story, every time I tell somebody this, they always, they love it, but I’m going to tell this so this will be on film forever. I will never forget, we were playing in a place and there was no one in the place, just like this room we’re in now, with the band. We were up there playing. And I was just like that [scats]. And he turned around and he leaned over the drum set at me and he said “what are you doing?” And I said “well…

“there’s nobody in here.” He looked me right in — I mean he got closer — he said “I’m here.” That was the scariest thing, I mean and the way he said it, you know what I mean? But it made a difference in me. He said “I’m here.” Let’s play. Because that’s what he did. I mean I’ve heard him play some of the greatest music I ever heard, in a room just like this with nobody in it. He loved that horn. It was just like — that’s why at his funeral, when Dizzy said, He said “y’all gotta find something else to do now,” he…
